[1/3] Plan: add the preview_blend_space2d editor action (x, y, time, record) with history support, editor document exposure, schema example/fields, action registration and a discovery flag, completing the 2D animation authoring loop

impact_assessment.why: ADR-240 made states drive a 2D space, but the editor could only scrub 1D, so people and AI clients could not preview 2D locomotion on the authoring surface.
impact_assessment.benefits: The editor applies a sampled 2D pose through undo history or unrecorded, reports axes/parameters, and both preview actions are documented in the API index and schema.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new editor action, editor document field, capability and schema entries; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: preview fields reset per action like the existing previews.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Mirror the 1D action's validation and history path, keep the schema example test green, reject non-finite coordinates and negative time before applying, and keep the canonical frame unchanged.

checkpoints.description: [1/3] Plan (impact-assessed): add preview_blend_space2d to the editor API with x/y/time/record, history support, editor document exposure, schema example and fields, action registration and animation_preview_blend_2d

impact_assessment.why: ADR-240 made states drive a 2D space, but the editor could only scrub 1D, so people and AI clients could not preview 2D locomotion on the authoring surface.
impact_assessment.benefits: A sampled 2D pose applies through undo history or unrecorded, with axes and parameters reported, and both preview actions are discoverable from the API index, schema and describe payload.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new editor action, editor field, capability and schema entries; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: preview records reset per action as the existing previews do.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Mirror the 1D validation and history path, keep the schema example test green, reject non-finite coordinates and negative time before applying, and keep the canonical frame unchanged.

[1/3] Plan: add pure deterministic steering (Agent, seek, arrive, separation, steer, steering_report) that shapes wish velocities from navigation into collision-avoiding movement, with quadratic contact repulsion, max-speed clamping and a discovery flag

impact_assessment.why: Navigation routes and PathFollower wishes existed, but nothing kept multiple agents apart; physics pushout is after-the-fact and a full velocity-obstacle solver would be large and hard to verify.
impact_assessment.benefits: Games can shape a wish velocity around neighbours without a dependency, the layer composes with PathFollower and CharacterController, and AI clients get a JSON steering report.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new module, six exports and a capability; dependency: none; concurrency: pure functions; state: frozen agents only.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep functions pure and caller-ordered, validate finite inputs, use quadratic falloff with a deterministic coincident rule, pin seek/arrive/separation/clamps, and keep the canonical evidence unchanged.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Implemented and verified - keystone/steering.py adds frozen Agent, seek, arrive, separation (quadratic contact falloff with a deterministic coincident rule), steer (identity skip, weighted separation, max-speed clamp) and steering_report; exports, README section and bullet, ARCHITECTURE row and tree, docs/TREE, CHANGELOG and ADR-242 updated; --describe reports capabilities.steering; 21 tests green (1246 collected), ruff clean, aikit check keystone 6/6 gates, canonical hash 772cac5232a0947b8f6d1914a5cf0cde and 4899-byte reference PNG unchanged; checklists: passed
Task 'keystone-steering-v1' completed successfully.

[1/3] Plan: add immutable tile maps (TileMap, tilemap_report) with exact per-cell AABB colliders, a merged floor-and-wall MeshData in one draw, with_cell copies, schema-1 documents and a discovery flag

impact_assessment.why: A grid level still had to be assembled by hand from nodes and colliders; navigation authoring already treats blockers as cell data, so one authored tile map is the missing form shared by rendering, physics and navigation.
impact_assessment.benefits: One document and one node produce a level, collision and navigation input from the same cells, with deterministic order and reports for AI clients.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new module, two exports and a capability; dependency: tilemap uses mesh_builder and physics.AABB; concurrency: none; state: schema-1 document is new and does not touch scene snapshots.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep the map immutable, validate cells/colors/geometry strictly, prove mesh counts/normals/bounds and a physics ray, and keep the canonical evidence unchanged.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Implemented and verified - keystone/tilemap.py adds immutable TileMap with cell math, with_cell copies, per-cell AABB colliders in x-major order, a merged floor-quad/wall-box MeshData (28 verts and 14 tris for one free plus one solid cell) facing up and spanning the wall height, schema-1 documents with strict validation and tilemap_report; exports, README section and scene bullet, ARCHITECTURE row and tree, docs/TREE, CHANGELOG and ADR-243 updated; --describe reports capabilities.tilemap; 14 tilemap tests green including a physics ray against the colliders (1260 collected), ruff clean, aikit check keystone 6/6 gates, canonical hash 772cac5232a0947b8f6d1914a5cf0cde and 4899-byte reference PNG unchanged; checklists: passed
Task 'keystone-tilemap-v1' completed successfully.

[1/3] Plan: add inspect_tilemap and build_tilemap editor actions with schema examples and fields, editor document exposure, undo-aware mesh application and discovery through the registered action list

impact_assessment.why: TileMap documents and meshes existed but the authoring surface could not inspect or apply them without Python.
impact_assessment.benefits: A tile-map document is validated, summarized and applied to a node through undo history from the same JSON API an AI already uses.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: two editor actions, editor fields and schema entries; dependency: web server imports keystone.tilemap; concurrency: session lock; state: one-shot result fields reset per action.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Validate the document and node before any change, apply the mesh through _apply_history, pin undo accounting and error paths, and keep the canonical frame unchanged.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Implemented and verified - inspect_tilemap reports a schema-1 tile map's counts and bounds; build_tilemap resolves a node, assigns the merged mesh through undo history and reports vertices, triangles, colliders and the map report; both actions are registered, have schema examples and field lists, and the editor document exposes tilemap and tilemap_build; README, ARCHITECTURE, CHANGELOG and ADR-244 updated; 1261 tests green (1 new web test), ruff clean, aikit check keystone 6/6 gates, canonical hash 772cac5232a0947b8f6d1914a5cf0cde and 4899-byte reference PNG unchanged; checklists: passed
Task 'keystone-editor-tilemap-v1' completed successfully.

[1/3] Plan: add an opt-in Reinhard/ACES tonemap to PostSettings, shaders and renderer plumbing, persist it through snapshots, scene export and the editor set_scene action, report it in renderer stats, and advertise post_tonemap

impact_assessment.why: The post grade clipped bright emissive values to white and the roadmap still listed the full post chain; a tonemap is the part that fits the existing single-pass grade.
impact_assessment.benefits: Three distinguishable roll-off modes with a default that leaves every existing frame unchanged, authorable from Python, snapshots and the editor, and visible in reports.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: PostSettings field, scene export schema 3, editor schema 60, shader uniforms; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: additive snapshot field with a default.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Default none keeps the canonical frame byte-identical, validate at construction/editor/snapshot, pin rendered brightness for all three modes, and run the strict gates.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Implemented and verified - PostSettings.tone (none/reinhard/aces) validates; the standard, sprite and sky shaders apply exposure then tone then vignette; renderer threads tone and reports post_tone; snapshots, scene export (schema 3), editor set_scene/editor document (schema 60) carry it; README, ARCHITECTURE, CHANGELOG and ADR-245 updated; --describe reports capabilities.post_tonemap; a rendered emissive surface is brighter with none than reinhard, aces differs, and disabled post ignores tone; 1266 tests green, ruff clean, aikit check keystone 6/6 gates, canonical hash 772cac5232a0947b8f6d1914a5cf0cde and 4899-byte reference PNG unchanged; checklists: passed
Task 'keystone-tonemap-v1' completed successfully.

[1/3] Plan: make post exposure and vignette per-scene settings (defaults 1.12 and 0.28), persist them through snapshots, scene export and editor set_scene, report them in renderer stats, and keep the canonical frame identical

impact_assessment.why: The tonemap was configurable but exposure and vignette stayed compile-time constants, so games could not tune grade brightness or corner falloff and AI clients could not diff them.
impact_assessment.benefits: Authorable grade controls from Python, snapshots and the editor, visible in reports, with defaults that preserve every existing frame.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: two PostSettings fields, scene export schema 4 and editor schema 61; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: additive snapshot fields with defaults.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Validate ranges at construction/editor/load, pin rendered brightness and corner darkening, keep defaults equal to the constants, and run strict gates.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Implemented and verified - PostSettings.exposure (finite, non-negative, default 1.12) and vignette (0..1, default 0.28) validate; the renderer, sky and sprite passes read scene values and stats report post_exposure/post_vignette; snapshots, scene export (schema 4), editor document/set_scene (schema 61) carry both; CPU defaults match POST_EXPOSURE/POST_VIGNETTE; exposure 2.0 renders brighter and vignette 1.0 darkens the corner while 0.0 does not; disable post still ignores both; 1272 tests green, ruff clean, aikit check keystone 6/6 gates, canonical hash 772cac5232a0947b8f6d1914a5cf0cde and 4899-byte reference PNG unchanged; checklists: passed
